info.title: Knee MRI preprocessed slice stacks, part 1 of 2
info.subtitle: Axial knee-MRI studies resampled into fixed-size volume stacks, ready to train.
info.description:
![Dread Development — Johnathan Wagner](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/dread-orbit-web.webp)

[![Kaggle](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/kaggle-bar.png)](https://www.kaggle.com/dreaddevelopment) [![GitHub](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/github-bar.png)](https://github.com/Bojackdidit) [![Website](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/website-bar.png)](https://dreaddevelopment.com) [![Email](https://bojackdidit.github.io/dread-cinematic-banner/buttons/email-bar.png)](mailto:john@dreaddevelopment.com)

Part 1 of 2. Holds the first 3,200 studies. Part 2 (knee-raptor-corpus-ext) holds the remaining 1,207; you need both for the full 4,407.

Every study in this competition arrives as a handful of DICOM series shot in different planes, and
no two studies match: the number of series varies, and the number of slices per series varies more.
Anything that expects a fixed-size input has to be given one. This is that fixed input, precomputed,
so you can train a model without touching a single DICOM.

HOW EACH STUDY WAS REDUCED

Every study becomes a stack of 44 images at 336 x 336, held as uint8. The 44 slots are filled in a
fixed order:

  12 slices from a sagittal series, preferring a fluid-sensitive one
  10 slices from a second sagittal series, preferring one that is not fluid-sensitive
   8 slices from a coronal series, preferring a fluid-sensitive one
   6 slices from a second coronal series
   8 slices from an axial series

Preferring fluid-sensitive sequences for some slots and not others is deliberate. Fluid-sensitive
sequences show swelling, effusion and acute injury clearly, while the others show anatomy and
cartilage better, and the findings are split across both. Where a study has no series for a slot,
the slot is left as zeros and the mask marks it, so a model can skip it rather than be fed
something misleading.

Within a series, slices are taken evenly across 15 to 85 percent of the stack. Each slice is
cropped to a 140 mm box around the image centre using the pixel spacing from the DICOM header, then
resized to 336 pixels. Cropping by millimetres rather than by pixel count matters: a knee then fills
the same fraction of the frame whether the scan was acquired at 0.3 or 0.5 mm per pixel, so the
model is not asked to learn scale differences that carry no medical information.

⛔ ROW ORDER IS THE CONTRACT. The ids file defines row i of the volumes file. Never sort or reindex
one without the other.

WHAT THIS CORPUS IS NOT

These stacks use 15 to 85 percent of each series. Later work found that widening that span to 6 to
94 percent, and sampling more densely, both scored better on the leaderboard, so this is the
starting geometry rather than the best one found. The published inference notebook shows how the
same preprocessing is done at other settings, and the slot table and crop are unchanged, so it is
straightforward to rebuild at a different span or slice count.

Labels are not included here. The competition provides structured labels for only 58 of the 4,407
studies; the rest carry a free-text radiology report instead.

FILES

  all_vols.npy      (3200, 44, 336, 336) uint8. Load with mmap_mode='r'; it is 15.9 GB.
  all_masks.npy     (3200, 44) uint8. 1 where the slot holds a real slice, 0 where it is empty.
  all_ids.npy       (3200,) StudyInstanceUID strings. Row i names row i of all_vols.npy.
  window_index.npy  helper index over usable 3-slice window positions.
